blocks.content: The Competition Commission of India possesses powers equivalent to a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 while trying a suit.

rows: Inquire into anti-competitive agreements or abuse of dominant position (suo motu or on information)
Pass Cease & Desist orders, modify agreements, and levy penalty up to 10% average turnover
Order division of enterprise enjoying dominant position to ensure fair competition
Issue temporary injunctions against anti-competitive practices during pending inquiry

items: Frequently asked penalty rule: Under Section 27, maximum monetary penalty is capped at 10% of the average turnover for the preceding three financial years.
Procedural jurisdiction: Under Section 36, CCI has powers to summon witnesses, examine on oath, require discovery of documents, and requisition public records.
Interim Order Section: Section 33 allows CCI to pass temporary injunctions before completing the full inquiry.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) holds statutory powers under Section 19 to inquire into anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominant position.
Section 27 empowers CCI to pass 'Cease and Desist' orders and impose monetary penalties up to 10% of the average turnover of the preceding three financial years.
Under Section 36, CCI is vested with the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 regarding summoning, discovery, and receiving evidence.
Section 28 allows CCI to direct the structural division of an enterprise enjoying a dominant position to prevent its abuse.
Section 33 grants CCI the power to issue interim orders to temporarily restrain any party from carrying out anti-competitive acts during an ongoing inquiry.
